findings.title: Managed-files write APIs bypass #57505 sensitive-path guard, allowing overwrite of .env and SSH keys
findings.description: PR #57505 added _is_sensitive_path() to managed-files READ/LIST/DOWNLOAD only. Writers (upload, stream upload, mkdir, delete) omit the guard; the module docstring states write was left unprotected. With default local FilesPolicy (locked_root=None), absolute/tilde paths under $HOME are allowed, so dashboard JWT holders can overwrite .env, auth.json, and ~/.ssh/authorized_keys while the parallel read path correctly returns 403 for the same paths.
findings.impact: An authenticated dashboard user can replace Hermes credentials or plant SSH authorized_keys despite the sensitive-path protection that blocks reading those same files — credential injection and host persistence from the dashboard files UI.
findings.attack_path:
1. Obtain a dashboard JWT (loopback token or stolen session).
2. Confirm GET /api/files/read?path=<home>/.hermes/.env returns 403 (sensitive-path guard works on read).
3. POST /api/files/upload with the same path and attacker-controlled body; receive 200 and overwrite .
4. Optionally POST /api/files/upload-stream, POST /api/files/mkdir, or DELETE /api/files/delete for the same class of paths under unlocked local policy.
findings.remediation: Call _is_sensitive_path (and ideally agent.file_safety write denylist) in upload_managed_file, upload_managed_file_stream, create_managed_directory, and delete_managed_file before open()/unlink()/mkdir. Add tests mirroring test_api_files_read_blocks_sensitive_env_file for upload/delete/mkdir.
findings.poc_video_notes: Reproduced under isolated HOME/HERMES_HOME: GET /api/files/read on .env returned 403; POST /api/files/upload overwrote .env with 200; ~/.ssh/authorized_keys upload also 200 under unlocked local FilesPolicy.

findings.title: MCP dashboard add/test probes attacker-controlled HTTP URLs without SSRF controls
findings.description: POST /api/mcp/servers and POST /api/mcp/servers/{name}/test pass user-supplied url into httpx HEAD/GET/POST via _probe_single_server with no is_safe_url or create_ssrf_safe_* client. Distinct from the already-reported provider-probe SSRF. MCP stdio command launch is intentional operator RCE and out of scope; this finding covers HTTP/SSE URL probing only.
findings.impact: A dashboard JWT holder can coerce the Hermes host to request IMDS or internal HTTP services; probe errors and response bodies surface in the test/save API response, enabling metadata or internal service data leakage.
findings.attack_path:
1. Authenticate to the dashboard.
2. POST /api/mcp/servers with transport http and url http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ (or POST .../test for an existing server).
3. Server issues outbound HEAD then POST initialize to that URL via plain httpx.
4. Attacker observes reachability and any returned body/errors from the probe response.
findings.remediation: Reject unsafe URLs with is_safe_url before probe/connect; use create_ssrf_safe_async_client for HTTP MCP transports at config save and test time.
findings.poc_video_notes: PoC loopback HTTP server received HEAD + POST /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ from _save_mcp_server and _probe_single_server under isolated HERMES_HOME.
